description: Acupuncture treatment by a licensed acupuncturist. Involves inserting thin needles into specific body points to relieve pain, manage stress, or treat various conditions. Common for chronic pain, migraines, back pain, and muscle tension. Students often seek this for stress-related tension and sports injuries.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Allied Health

description: An aerochamber or spacer device used with metered-dose inhalers (MDIs) to improve medication delivery to the lungs. Commonly used by asthma or COPD patients to ensure proper inhalation of prescribed medication. The chamber holds the aerosolized medicine so the patient can inhale it more effectively.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Respiratory Equipment

description: Sterile alcohol swabs or prep pads used for disinfecting skin before injections, blood glucose testing, or wound care. Commonly needed by diabetic patients for daily insulin injections or blood sugar monitoring. Also used for general first aid and medical procedures at home.
benefit_type: Prescription Drugs / Medical Supplies

description: Professional ambulance transportation service for medical emergencies. Covers land or air ambulance to the nearest equipped hospital when medically required due to injury, illness, or acute physical disability. Typically used in emergency situations like accidents, sudden illness, or severe injuries.
benefit_type: Emergency Transportation

description: A 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring test where a portable device measures blood pressure at regular intervals throughout the day and night. Used to diagnose hypertension, white coat syndrome, or monitor blood pressure medication effectiveness. The patient wears the device during normal daily activities.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: Treatment by a certified athletic therapist for musculoskeletal injuries and conditions. Focuses on prevention, assessment, and rehabilitation of sports injuries and orthopedic conditions. Common for student athletes dealing with sprains, strains, concussions, and rehabilitation from sports-related injuries.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Allied Health

description: Services provided by a licensed audiologist for hearing assessment, management, and rehabilitation. Includes hearing evaluations, hearing aid fittings, tinnitus management, and balance disorder assessment. Different from audiometric exam which is specifically the hearing test itself.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Hearing

description: A diagnostic audiometric examination to test hearing acuity. Measures the ability to hear sounds at different pitches and volumes. Used to detect hearing loss, determine its type and severity. Typically performed in a sound booth by an audiologist or hearing specialist.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Hearing

description: Purchase of a bath bench or shower chair for safe bathing. An assistive device placed in the bathtub or shower to allow a person to sit while bathing. Used by individuals with mobility limitations, balance issues, or post-surgery recovery who cannot safely stand in the shower.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Aids for Daily Living
benefit_group: Medical Items - Aids for Daily Living

description: Purchase of bed rails or safety rails that attach to a hospital or home bed. Provides support for getting in and out of bed and prevents falls during sleep. Used by individuals with mobility challenges, post-surgery patients, or those at risk of falling out of bed.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Aids for Daily Living
benefit_group: Medical Items - Aids for Daily Living

description: A bedpan used for toileting by individuals who are bedridden or unable to get to the bathroom. A medical device placed under or beside a patient in bed for collecting urine or feces. Used during recovery from surgery, illness, or for individuals with severe mobility limitations.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Aids for Daily Living
benefit_group: Medical Items - Aids for Daily Living

description: A blood glucose meter (glucometer) device used to measure blood sugar levels. A portable electronic device that reads blood glucose concentration from a small blood sample, typically from a finger prick. Essential for diabetic patients to monitor their blood sugar daily. This is the meter device itself, not the continuous monitoring system.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diabetic Supplies

description: A home blood pressure monitor device for self-monitoring of blood pressure. An electronic device with an arm cuff that measures systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Used by patients with hypertension or those who need regular blood pressure tracking at home.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Respiratory/Cardiology Equipment

category: Blood test for Allergies (IG test not eligible)
description: A blood test to identify allergies, typically an IgE blood test (immunoglobulin E). Note that IG tests are not eligible for coverage. Used to identify specific allergens causing allergic reactions such as food allergies, environmental allergies, or drug allergies. Different from a scratch/skin test for allergies.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests
disambiguation_attributes: blood draw test not skin test

description: The fee charged for drawing blood (venipuncture or phlebotomy). This covers the professional fee for a nurse or phlebotomist to draw blood for laboratory testing. Separate from the cost of the actual lab tests themselves. Common when getting blood work done at a clinic or lab.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: A non-custom (off-the-shelf) orthopedic brace for supporting or immobilizing a body part. Includes wrist braces, ankle braces, back braces, elbow braces, and other pre-made support devices. Purchased from a pharmacy or medical supply store without custom fitting. Used for sprains, strains, arthritis support, or post-injury stabilization.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Braces and Casts

description: A custom-made ankle-foot orthosis (AFO) or knee-ankle-foot orthosis (KAFO). These are specialized orthopedic devices custom-fitted to support the ankle, foot, and/or knee. Used for conditions like drop foot, post-stroke rehabilitation, cerebral palsy, or other neuromuscular conditions affecting the lower limbs.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Braces and Casts

description: A custom-made knee brace specifically for the left knee. Custom-fitted and manufactured for the individual patient's left knee anatomy. Used for conditions like ACL/MCL injuries, knee osteoarthritis, post-surgical knee support, or chronic knee instability. Must specify left knee when submitting claim.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Braces and Casts

description: A custom-made knee brace specifically for the right knee. Custom-fitted and manufactured for the individual patient's right knee anatomy. Used for conditions like ACL/MCL injuries, knee osteoarthritis, post-surgical knee support, or chronic knee instability. Must specify right knee when submitting claim.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Braces and Casts

description: Purchase of a breast pump for expressing breast milk. Can be manual or electric. Used by breastfeeding mothers to express and store milk for feeding infants. Useful for working mothers, those with latching difficulties, or to maintain milk supply.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services

description: A CA-125 blood test that measures the level of cancer antigen 125 protein in the blood. Primarily used as a tumor marker for ovarian cancer screening, diagnosis, and monitoring treatment response. May also be elevated in endometriosis, uterine fibroids, and other conditions.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: A standard walking cane for mobility assistance. A single-point cane used by individuals who need balance support or weight-bearing assistance while walking. Different from a quad cane which has four feet. Used after injury, surgery, or for chronic mobility conditions.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Mobility Aids

description: A fiberglass cast used to immobilize and protect a broken or fractured bone while it heals. Lighter and more durable than traditional plaster casts. Applied by a healthcare professional after fracture reduction. Common for broken arms, wrists, legs, and ankles.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Braces and Casts

description: A cervical pillow designed to support the natural curve of the neck during sleep. An orthopedic pillow that helps maintain proper spinal alignment and reduces neck pain. Used for cervical spondylosis, neck strain, whiplash recovery, or chronic neck pain management.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services

description: Foot care treatment by a licensed chiropodist. Includes assessment and treatment of foot conditions such as corns, calluses, ingrown toenails, plantar warts, and diabetic foot care. Chiropody focuses on the treatment of foot ailments, distinct from podiatry which may include surgical interventions. Does not include orthotics or orthopedic shoes.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Foot Care

description: Chiropractic treatment by a licensed chiropractor. Involves spinal adjustments, joint manipulation, and other manual therapies to treat musculoskeletal conditions. Common for back pain, neck pain, headaches, and joint problems. One of the most frequently claimed professional services by students.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group A

description: Mental health counselling services by a registered clinical counsellor (RCC). Provides therapy for anxiety, depression, stress, relationship issues, grief, trauma, and other mental health concerns. A clinical counsellor has specific training in therapeutic counselling techniques. Part of the mental health practitioner group alongside psychologists and social workers.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group B

description: Purchase of reusable cold therapy items for pain and inflammation management. Includes reusable ice packs, cold wraps, gel packs, and cold therapy systems. Used for acute injuries, post-surgery swelling, sprains, strains, and chronic pain management. Must be reusable, not single-use disposable products.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services

description: A colonoscopy procedure - an examination of the large intestine (colon) using a flexible camera scope. Used for colorectal cancer screening, investigating digestive symptoms like blood in stool, chronic diarrhea, or abdominal pain. Also used for polyp detection and removal. Usually performed by a gastroenterologist.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: Compression calf sleeves or tights that are footless - they do not cover the foot. Any length available. These are sleeve-style compression garments worn on the calf/leg without a foot portion. Used for circulation support, varicose veins, or athletic recovery. Different from compression stockings which include the foot.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Compression Stockings

category: Compression Stockings, any length (up to 14 mmhg)
description: Compression stockings of any length with pressure up to 14 mmHg (light compression). These are low-pressure support stockings for mild circulation issues or prevention. Note: the booklet requires 15 mmHg or higher for coverage, so these light-compression stockings may not be eligible under the plan.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Compression Stockings
disambiguation_attributes: may not meet minimum 15 mmHg requirement

description: Custom-made compression stockings of any length and pressure level. These are individually measured and manufactured to fit the patient's specific leg dimensions. Prescribed for chronic venous insufficiency, lymphedema, severe varicose veins, or post-surgical recovery. More expensive than off-the-shelf but provide better fit and pressure distribution.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Compression Stockings

description: Knee-length compression stockings with 15-19 mmHg pressure (mild-to-moderate compression). Off-the-shelf stockings that extend to just below the knee. Used for mild varicose veins, tired/aching legs, mild swelling, and long travel. The lowest pressure level that meets the plan's 15 mmHg minimum requirement.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Compression Stockings

description: Knee-length compression stockings with 20-29 mmHg pressure (moderate compression). Off-the-shelf stockings extending to just below the knee. Used for moderate varicose veins, edema, post-sclerotherapy, mild lymphedema, and DVT prevention. A commonly prescribed compression level for medical conditions.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Compression Stockings

category: Compression Stockings, knee length (30 mmhg & over)
description: Knee-length compression stockings with 30 mmHg or higher pressure (firm to extra-firm compression). Off-the-shelf stockings extending to just below the knee. Used for severe varicose veins, severe edema, active venous ulcers, post-thrombotic syndrome, and severe lymphedema. Highest compression level in knee length.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Compression Stockings

description: Thigh-length or full-length compression stockings with 15-19 mmHg pressure (mild-to-moderate compression). Off-the-shelf stockings extending to the thigh or waist. Used for mild varicose veins in the upper leg, mild edema, and prevention during pregnancy or long travel.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Compression Stockings

description: Thigh-length or full-length compression stockings with 20-29 mmHg pressure (moderate compression). Off-the-shelf stockings extending to the thigh or waist. Used for moderate varicose veins, post-surgical edema, DVT prevention, and lymphedema management in the full leg.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Compression Stockings

description: Thigh-length or full-length compression stockings with 30 mmHg or higher pressure (firm to extra-firm compression). Off-the-shelf stockings extending to the thigh or waist. Used for severe venous insufficiency, severe lymphedema, active venous ulcers, and post-thrombotic syndrome in the full leg.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Compression Stockings

description: A CPAP (Continuous Positive Airway Pressure), APAP (Automatic Positive Airway Pressure), or BIPAP (Bilevel Positive Airway Pressure) machine for treating sleep apnea. The machine itself delivers pressurized air through a mask to keep airways open during sleep. This is for the machine/device only, not the mask or other supplies.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Respiratory Equipment

description: A mask for CPAP, APAP, or BIPAP machine used in sleep apnea treatment. The mask fits over the nose, mouth, or both and connects to the machine via tubing. Types include nasal mask, full face mask, and nasal pillow mask. This is specifically for the mask component, not the machine or other supplies.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Respiratory Equipment
disambiguation_attributes: not other supplies like tubing or filters

description: Supplies and accessories for CPAP, APAP, or BIPAP machines, excluding the machine and mask themselves. Includes tubing, filters, humidifier chambers, chin straps, headgear, water chambers, and replacement parts. These consumable items need regular replacement for proper machine function and hygiene.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Respiratory Equipment

description: A pair of standard underarm (axillary) crutches for mobility assistance after lower limb injury or surgery. Traditional crutches that go under the armpits with hand grips. Used for fractures, sprains, post-surgical recovery, or other conditions requiring non-weight-bearing or partial weight-bearing on a leg. This is for a standard pair, not forearm crutches.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Mobility Aids

description: Custom-made orthotic insoles or inserts for shoes, individually designed and manufactured based on a cast, mold, or 3D scan of the patient's feet. Prescribed by a podiatrist, chiropodist, or other qualified practitioner for conditions like plantar fasciitis, flat feet, high arches, overpronation, or diabetic foot care. More expensive than standard inserts but tailored to individual biomechanical needs.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Foot Care

description: Dental treatment for teeth damaged in an accident - specifically a direct blow to the mouth that damages natural teeth. Covers emergency dental care, repair, or replacement of natural teeth injured in an accident. Must notify GreenShield immediately after the accident. Treatment must begin within 180 days. Does not cover damage from biting on objects.
benefit_type: Accidental Dental

description: A pre-treatment dental estimate or predetermination submitted to GreenShield before dental work is done. Used to confirm coverage and expected reimbursement amount before committing to expensive dental procedures. The dentist prepares an estimate of proposed treatment and costs, which is submitted for approval. Recommended for procedures over a certain cost threshold.
benefit_type: Dental Services

description: General dental services including routine exams, cleanings, fillings, extractions, X-rays, and other basic to comprehensive dental treatments. This is the catch-all category for regular dental work not covered by more specific categories. Includes preventive care, basic restorative, oral surgery, and major services as outlined in the dental benefit plan.
benefit_type: Dental Services

description: A diagnostic vision test beyond a standard eye exam. Includes specialized testing such as visual field testing, optical coherence tomography (OCT), retinal imaging, corneal topography, or other diagnostic procedures to investigate eye diseases or conditions. Different from a routine eye exam which is for prescription updates.
benefit_type: Vision
disambiguation_attributes: not routine eye exam for glasses prescription

description: Nutritional counselling and dietary planning services provided by a registered dietitian (RD). Includes meal planning, nutritional assessment, dietary management for medical conditions like diabetes, celiac disease, food allergies, eating disorders, or weight management. Dietitians are regulated healthcare professionals different from nutritionists.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Allied Health

description: Online or app-based cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) programs. Digital mental health treatment that provides structured CBT techniques through a digital platform, often with therapist support. Used for anxiety, depression, insomnia, and other mental health conditions. Examples include programs like MindBeacon, BEACON, or similar digital CBT platforms.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group B
disambiguation_attributes: structured CBT program via app or website

description: Prescription drugs and medications prescribed by a physician or dentist. Covers medications that legally require a prescription and have a Drug Identification Number (DIN). Includes most prescribed medications, insulin, diabetic supplies, and some vaccines. Uses the Pay Direct Drug Card. Generic substitution is enforced unless the physician specifies no substitution.
benefit_type: Prescription Drugs

description: Custom-made ear plugs molded to fit the individual's ear canal. Made from impressions taken of the ears for a precise fit. Used for noise protection, swimming protection, sleep, musician ear plugs, or industrial noise environments. Different from off-the-shelf disposable ear plugs. Must be custom-made to qualify.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Hearing

description: A pre-authorization or estimate request submitted to GreenShield before receiving medical treatment or purchasing medical equipment. Used to confirm coverage eligibility and expected reimbursement before incurring costs. Required for certain expensive items like wheelchairs, hearing aids, or specific treatments. Different from dental estimate which is specific to dental procedures.
benefit_type: General - Administrative

description: A routine optometric eye examination to assess vision and check for eye health conditions. Includes refraction test for glasses/contact lens prescription, eye pressure measurement, and general eye health screening. Performed by an optometrist. Covered only in provinces where not covered by the provincial health plan. One exam every 2 years.
benefit_type: Vision
disambiguation_attributes: not diagnostic vision test for eye diseases

description: Purchase of a forearm crutch (also called elbow crutch or Lofstrand crutch). A crutch with a forearm cuff and hand grip, providing more stability and control than standard underarm crutches. Often used for long-term mobility needs, chronic conditions, or when upper body strength is limited. Different from standard underarm crutches.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Mobility Aids

description: The receiver device for a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system. This is the handheld display unit that receives data from the transmitter and shows real-time glucose readings. Part of a CGM system like Dexcom or Freestyle Libre. This is only the receiver/reader, not the transmitter or sensors.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diabetic Supplies

description: Supplies and sensors for a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system. Includes disposable sensor patches that are applied to the skin, adhesive patches, and other consumable supplies. These need regular replacement (typically every 7-14 days for sensors). Not the receiver or transmitter devices themselves.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diabetic Supplies

description: The transmitter component of a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system. This small device attaches to the sensor on the body and wirelessly sends glucose data to the receiver or smartphone. Part of a CGM system like Dexcom. Transmitters typically last several months before needing replacement. This is only the transmitter, not the receiver or sensors.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diabetic Supplies
disambiguation_attributes: sends data wirelessly from sensor to receiver

description: Purchase of grab bars or bath bars that are permanently installed as safety fixtures. Metal or plastic bars mounted to bathroom walls near the toilet, bathtub, or shower for support and fall prevention. Used by individuals with mobility challenges, balance issues, or elderly care. These are permanent fixtures requiring installation, not portable devices.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Aids for Daily Living
benefit_group: Medical Items - Aids for Daily Living

description: Hearing aid devices that amplify sound for individuals with hearing loss. Electronic devices worn in or behind the ear that make sounds louder and clearer. Includes behind-the-ear (BTE), in-the-ear (ITE), receiver-in-canal (RIC), and completely-in-canal (CIC) types. Requires audiologist assessment and fitting. Significant purchase typically requiring pre-authorization.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Hearing

description: Purchase of reusable heat therapy items for pain management and muscle relaxation. Includes reusable heat packs, heating pads, microwaveable heat wraps, hot water bottles, and similar devices. Used for muscle stiffness, chronic pain, menstrual cramps, arthritis, and muscle spasm relief. Must be reusable, not single-use disposable products.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services

description: Treatment by a licensed homeopath or homeopathic practitioner. Homeopathy is an alternative medicine system that uses highly diluted substances to trigger the body's natural healing response. Used for various conditions including allergies, chronic fatigue, digestive issues, and skin conditions. Must be a registered homeopathic practitioner.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Allied Health

description: Hospital accommodation charges within your province of residence. Covers semi-private room charges in a public hospital. Includes stays in general, convalescent, rehabilitation, or chronic hospitals. Coverage is 50% co-pay for up to 5 days per disability. This is for the room charges, not for procedures or treatments.
benefit_type: Hospital

description: A table-top humidifier for medical use, adding moisture to indoor air. Used for respiratory conditions like dry cough, sinus congestion, nosebleeds from dry air, and to complement CPAP therapy. A compact unit designed for bedside or desk use, not a whole-house system. May be recommended for patients with chronic respiratory conditions.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Respiratory Equipment

description: Home care and support services provided in the patient's home. Includes registered nursing care, personal care assistance, and health support services delivered at home rather than in a healthcare facility. For patients recovering from surgery, managing chronic conditions, or requiring ongoing medical care at home. Requires pre-authorization from a physician.
benefit_type: Private Duty Nursing in the Home

description: Medical supplies for managing urinary or fecal incontinence. Includes adult diapers, incontinence pads, protective underwear, bed pads, catheter supplies, and related products. Used by individuals with bladder control issues due to medical conditions, post-surgery, aging, or neurological conditions.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Incontinence/Ostomy

description: An automatic insulin injection device (insulin pen with automatic injection mechanism). Automatically inserts the needle and delivers insulin with the push of a button, making self-injection easier. Used by diabetic patients who have difficulty with manual injection. Different from manual insulin pens and insulin pumps.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diabetic Supplies

description: A manual insulin injection device or pen. The user manually pushes the plunger or dial to inject insulin. Standard insulin pens like NovoPen or similar devices. Used by diabetic patients for daily insulin injections. Requires manual operation unlike automatic insulin guns.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diabetic Supplies

description: An insulin infusion pump - a small electronic device that delivers continuous insulin through a thin tube (cannula) inserted under the skin. Provides both basal (continuous) and bolus (mealtime) insulin delivery. Used by Type 1 diabetic patients or Type 2 patients requiring intensive insulin therapy. A significant medical device different from injection pens.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diabetic Supplies

description: Consumable supplies for an insulin infusion pump. Includes infusion sets (tubing and cannula), reservoirs/cartridges, insertion devices, adhesive patches, and other consumables needed to operate an insulin pump. These supplies need regular replacement, typically every 2-3 days for infusion sets.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diabetic Supplies

description: An insulin pen injector device used for administering insulin. A pen-shaped device that holds an insulin cartridge and allows precise dosing. Commonly used devices include reusable pens (where cartridges are replaced) and disposable pre-filled pens. This is the pen device itself, for general insulin pen claims.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diabetic Supplies

description: Purchase of an intravenous (IV) stand or pole for home use. A wheeled stand that holds IV fluid bags at the proper height for gravity-fed intravenous infusion. Used by patients receiving IV medications, fluids, or nutrition at home. Part of aids for daily living for home care patients.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Aids for Daily Living
benefit_group: Medical Items - Aids for Daily Living

description: Lancets used with a lancing device for blood glucose testing. Small disposable needles that prick the finger to obtain a blood sample for glucose monitoring. Essential supply for diabetic patients who test their blood sugar regularly. Used with a spring-loaded lancing device for quick, relatively painless finger pricks.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diabetic Supplies

description: A mammogram - an X-ray examination of the breast used to screen for or diagnose breast cancer. Can be a screening mammogram (routine) or a diagnostic mammogram (to investigate a lump or abnormality). Performed at a radiology clinic or hospital. Recommended for women over 40 or those with higher risk factors.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: Massage therapy treatment by a registered massage therapist (RMT). Includes therapeutic massage for pain management, muscle tension, stress relief, injury rehabilitation, and overall wellness. Common types include deep tissue, Swedish, sports massage, and myofascial release. One of the most frequently claimed services by students. Requires treatment by a licensed RMT.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group A

description: A specialized bra designed for individuals who have had a mastectomy (surgical removal of breast tissue). Features pockets to hold breast prostheses and is designed for comfort and support after breast surgery. Used as part of post-mastectomy recovery and ongoing daily wear. May be considered under prosthetics or medical items.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Prosthetics

description: A MedicAlert bracelet or necklace that displays critical medical information for emergencies. Engraved with the wearer's medical conditions, allergies, and emergency contact information. Essential for individuals with severe allergies (anaphylaxis), diabetes, epilepsy, heart conditions, or other conditions requiring immediate medical attention in emergencies.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services

description: Medical cannabis (marijuana) prescribed by a physician for medical purposes. Used for conditions like chronic pain, nausea from chemotherapy, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, and PTSD. Note: Medical cannabis is explicitly listed as NOT covered under the GreenShield prescription drug plan. The category exists in the dropdown but claims will likely be denied.
benefit_type: Prescription Drugs (NOT COVERED)
disambiguation_attributes: explicitly not covered by the plan

description: A magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan - a diagnostic imaging procedure that uses magnetic fields and radio waves to create detailed images of organs and tissues. Used to diagnose or investigate conditions affecting the brain, spine, joints, abdomen, or other body areas. Often ordered when more detail than an X-ray or ultrasound can provide is needed. May involve long wait times in the public system, leading patients to seek private MRI.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: Treatment by a licensed naturopathic doctor (ND). Naturopathy uses natural therapies including herbal medicine, nutrition, hydrotherapy, and lifestyle counseling to support the body's healing. Used for digestive issues, hormonal balance, chronic fatigue, skin conditions, and general wellness. Must be a licensed naturopathic practitioner.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group A

category: Nursing Home and Long Term Care
description: Charges related to nursing home residence or long-term care facility. Covers costs associated with residing in a licensed nursing home or long-term care facility for individuals who require ongoing medical care and assistance with daily living. Different from in-home support services. Typically for chronic conditions requiring continuous professional care.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services

description: Occupational therapy (OT) services by a registered occupational therapist. Helps patients develop, recover, or maintain daily living and work skills after injury, illness, or disability. Includes assessment and treatment for fine motor skills, adaptive equipment training, workplace ergonomics, and rehabilitation for daily activities like dressing, cooking, and bathing.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Allied Health

category: Orthodontic Services (Braces - initial and monthly fee)
description: Orthodontic treatment services including dental braces, initial consultation and fitting fees, and monthly adjustment fees. Covers the straightening and alignment of teeth using braces, retainers, or other orthodontic appliances. Includes initial assessment, appliance installation, regular adjustments, and retainer fitting. A long-term dental treatment typically spanning 1-3 years.
benefit_type: Dental Services - Orthodontic

description: Orthopedic shoes or custom-made shoes designed for medical conditions. Specially constructed footwear for individuals with foot deformities, diabetic foot conditions, severe biomechanical issues, or post-surgical foot care. Custom-made from measurements or casts of the patient's feet. Different from standard shoes with orthotic inserts.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Foot Care

description: Treatment by a licensed osteopath or doctor of osteopathic medicine. Osteopathy uses manual therapy techniques including joint manipulation, stretching, and massage to treat musculoskeletal conditions. Focuses on the relationship between the body's structure and function. Used for back pain, neck pain, headaches, and joint problems.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Allied Health

description: Ostomy supplies and equipment for individuals with an ostomy (surgically created opening for waste elimination). Includes ostomy bags/pouches, skin barriers, flanges, adhesives, deodorizers, and related accessories. Used after colostomy, ileostomy, or urostomy surgery. These are ongoing consumable supplies that need regular replacement.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Incontinence/Ostomy

description: Emergency medical services not covered by other specific categories. May include emergency room fees, urgent care visits, emergency medical procedures, or other emergency-related costs not fitting into ambulance or hospital categories. A catch-all for miscellaneous emergency medical expenses.
benefit_type: Emergency Transportation / Medical Items
disambiguation_attributes: emergency services not in other categories

category: Other foot care services (i.e. orthopedic shoe modification)
description: Foot care services not covered by other specific categories, such as orthopedic shoe modifications, heel lifts, metatarsal pads, shoe adjustments for medical conditions, and other specialized foot care. The catch-all for foot-related services that are not treatment (chiropody/podiatry), orthotics, or complete orthopedic shoes.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Foot Care
disambiguation_attributes: not treatment, not orthotics, not complete shoes

category: Other garment brace services (i.e. compression gloves)
description: Garment brace services not covered by other specific categories, such as compression gloves, compression arm sleeves, abdominal binders, and other support garments. The catch-all for compression garments and braces that are not compression stockings or standard orthopedic braces.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Braces and Casts

description: Health specialist services not covered by other specific practitioner categories. A catch-all for visits to licensed health professionals who do not fall into the named categories like chiropractor, physiotherapist, psychologist, etc. May include kinesiologists, reflexologists, or other regulated practitioners.
benefit_type: Professional Services
disambiguation_attributes: practitioners not listed in other specific categories

description: Hearing-related services not covered by other specific hearing categories (audiologist, audiometric exam, hearing aids, custom ear plugs). May include hearing aid repairs, ear mold impressions, assistive listening devices, or other hearing-related professional services.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Hearing
disambiguation_attributes: hearing services not in other specific hearing categories

description: Laboratory and diagnostic tests not covered by other specific test categories (blood tests, MRI, ultrasound, mammogram, etc.). May include CT scans, bone density tests, pulmonary function tests, EEG, ECG, and other medical tests. The catch-all for diagnostic procedures not specifically listed.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests
disambiguation_attributes: diagnostic tests not in other specific categories

description: Medical items and devices not covered by other specific categories. A catch-all for miscellaneous medical equipment, devices, or supplies that do not fit into named categories. May include thermometers, nebulizers, pulse oximeters, or other health monitoring and treatment devices.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services
disambiguation_attributes: medical items not in other specific categories

description: Mental health services not covered by other specific mental health categories (psychologist, psychotherapist, social worker, clinical counsellor, digital CBT). May include art therapy, music therapy, group therapy programs, psychiatric nursing, or other therapeutic mental health services.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group B
disambiguation_attributes: mental health services not in other specific categories

description: Orthodontic or dental services not covered by other specific dental categories. Includes orthodontic records (X-rays, photographs, impressions taken for orthodontic treatment planning), dental appliances, night guards, mouth guards, and other specialized dental services.
benefit_type: Dental Services
disambiguation_attributes: specialized dental/orthodontic services not in other categories

description: Vision-related services and products not covered by other specific vision categories (eye exam, prescription glasses, prescription contacts, diagnostic vision test). May include safety glasses with prescription lenses, sports goggles, low vision aids, or other vision-related items and services.
benefit_type: Vision
disambiguation_attributes: vision items/services not in other specific categories

description: A peak flow meter - a portable device that measures how fast a person can blow air out of their lungs. Used primarily by asthma patients to monitor lung function and detect early signs of an asthma attack. Provides a peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) reading. A simple, low-cost device for daily home monitoring.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Respiratory Equipment

description: Physiotherapy treatment by a licensed physiotherapist. Includes assessment and treatment of physical conditions through exercise, manual therapy, modalities (ultrasound, electrical stimulation), and education. Used for injury rehabilitation, post-surgical recovery, chronic pain management, sports injuries, and movement disorders. One of the most commonly claimed professional services.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group A

description: Foot care treatment by a licensed podiatrist (doctor of podiatric medicine). Podiatrists can diagnose and treat foot and ankle conditions including bunions, heel pain, plantar fasciitis, ingrown toenails, foot infections, and sports injuries. May include minor surgical procedures. Different from chiropody which focuses on general foot care.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Foot Care

description: Prescription contact lenses for vision correction. Includes soft contact lenses, rigid gas-permeable lenses, toric lenses for astigmatism, multifocal contacts, and medically necessary contact lenses for conditions like keratoconus. Prescribed by an optometrist or ophthalmologist. Coverage of $150 per 24 months combined with prescription glasses.
benefit_type: Vision

description: Prescription eyeglasses for vision correction. Includes frames and lenses prescribed by an optometrist or ophthalmologist. Covers single vision, bifocal, progressive, and other prescription lens types. Also includes replacement parts for prescription glasses. Coverage of $150 per 24 months combined with prescription contacts.
benefit_type: Vision

description: Coverage or reimbursement related to provincial health insurance plan replacement or coordination. Used when a service is typically covered by the provincial health plan but needs to be claimed through the private insurance instead. May apply when provincial coverage is not available or has been exhausted.
benefit_type: General - Administrative

description: A PSA blood test that measures the level of prostate-specific antigen in the blood. Used as a screening test for prostate cancer or to monitor prostate health. Elevated PSA levels may indicate prostate cancer, benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), or prostatitis. Typically recommended for men over 50 or those with risk factors.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: Mental health therapy provided by a registered psychologist (PhD or PsyD). Psychologists provide assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of mental health conditions through various therapeutic approaches including CBT, psychodynamic therapy, and behavioral therapy. Treats anxiety, depression, PTSD, OCD, and other psychological conditions. Higher qualification level than counsellors or psychotherapists.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group B

description: Mental health therapy by a registered psychotherapist. Provides talk therapy and therapeutic interventions for emotional and mental health conditions. Psychotherapists use various therapeutic modalities to help with anxiety, depression, relationship issues, trauma, and personal growth. Different from psychologists (who can do assessments/diagnosis) and counsellors.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group B

description: Purchase of a quad cane - a walking cane with a four-footed base for extra stability. Provides more support than a standard single-point cane, standing upright on its own when released. Used by individuals who need significant balance support but do not require a walker. Good for stroke recovery, balance disorders, or significant mobility limitations.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Mobility Aids

description: Purchase of a raised toilet seat that adds height to a standard toilet. Makes sitting down and standing up easier for individuals with hip, knee, or back problems, or those recovering from surgery. May come with handles/armrests for additional support. An aid for daily living that helps maintain independence in the bathroom.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Aids for Daily Living
benefit_group: Medical Items - Aids for Daily Living

description: Safety glasses for eye protection, potentially with prescription lenses. Protective eyewear designed to shield eyes from hazards in work, lab, or sports environments. May include prescription safety glasses for those who need vision correction while wearing protective eyewear. Different from regular prescription glasses or sunglasses.
benefit_type: Vision

description: A scratch test (skin prick test) for identifying allergies. Small amounts of suspected allergens are placed on the skin (usually the forearm or back), and the skin is lightly scratched. Positive reactions appear as raised bumps. Tests for environmental allergies, food allergies, and other allergens. Different from blood tests for allergies.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: Genetic screening or DNA testing for medical purposes. Includes genetic testing to identify inherited conditions, carrier status, or genetic risk factors for diseases. Used for conditions like BRCA gene testing for breast cancer risk, genetic counseling, carrier screening for family planning, or pharmacogenomic testing for medication response.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: A sleep study (polysomnography) to diagnose sleep disorders. Monitors brain activity, eye movements, heart rate, breathing patterns, and oxygen levels during sleep. Used to diagnose sleep apnea, insomnia, narcolepsy, restless leg syndrome, and other sleep disorders. Can be done in a sleep lab (in-lab) or at home (home sleep test).
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: Mental health services provided by a registered social worker with a Bachelor's degree (BSW). Provides counselling, case management, and support for mental health, relationship, and social issues. A bachelor-level social worker may have different scope of practice than a master-level social worker in some jurisdictions. Part of the mental health practitioner group.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group B
disambiguation_attributes: social worker not counsellor or psychologist

description: Mental health services provided by a registered social worker with a Master's degree (MSW). Master's-level social workers have advanced clinical training and broader scope of practice for psychotherapy and clinical assessment. Provides individual and group therapy, clinical assessment, crisis intervention, and specialized mental health treatment. Higher qualification than BSW.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group B

description: Speech therapy services by a licensed speech-language pathologist (SLP). Treats communication disorders including speech articulation, language development, stuttering, voice disorders, and swallowing difficulties (dysphagia). Used for stroke recovery, developmental delays, head injury recovery, and neurological conditions affecting speech.
benefit_type: Professional Services Group A

category: Standard foot orthotics or shoe inserts
description: Off-the-shelf (non-custom) foot orthotics or shoe inserts for foot support. Pre-made arch supports, insoles, or orthotic inserts purchased from a pharmacy or shoe store without custom fitting. Used for mild arch support, cushioning, or minor foot discomfort. Less expensive than custom orthotics but not individually tailored.
benefit_type: Professional Services - Foot Care

description: Purchase of a stationary commode - a portable toilet chair that does not have wheels. Placed beside a bed or in a room for individuals who have difficulty reaching the bathroom. Used by patients who are bedridden, recovering from surgery, or have severe mobility limitations. Different from a wheeled commode or raised toilet seat.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Aids for Daily Living
benefit_group: Medical Items - Aids for Daily Living

description: A TENS (Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation) unit or muscle/nerve stimulator device. Delivers low-voltage electrical impulses through the skin to relieve pain. Used for chronic pain, back pain, arthritis, fibromyalgia, and post-surgical pain management. This is the device itself, not the supplies/pads/electrodes.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services

description: Supplies and accessories for a TENS or muscle/nerve stimulator device. Includes electrode pads, lead wires, batteries, conductive gel, and replacement parts. These consumable items need regular replacement for the stimulator to function properly. This is for supplies only, not the stimulator device itself.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services

description: A tuberculosis (TB) skin test, also called a Mantoux test or PPD test (purified protein derivative). A small amount of tuberculin is injected under the skin of the forearm, and the area is checked 48-72 hours later for a reaction. Used to screen for latent TB infection. Often required for healthcare workers, students in health programs, or international students.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: A transport wheelchair - a lightweight wheelchair designed to be pushed by a caregiver rather than self-propelled by the user. Has smaller wheels than a standard wheelchair. Used for transporting patients who cannot walk long distances but do not need a full self-propelling wheelchair. Good for medical appointments, travel, or occasional use.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Mobility Aids

description: An ultrasound diagnostic imaging procedure that uses high-frequency sound waves to create images of internal body structures. Used for examining organs, muscles, tendons, and blood vessels. Common uses include pregnancy monitoring, abdominal imaging, thyroid evaluation, musculoskeletal assessment, and cardiac evaluation (echocardiogram).
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: Purchase of a urinal for home medical use. A container used for urination by individuals who are bedridden or have difficulty reaching the bathroom. Available in male and female designs. Part of aids for daily living for patients with mobility limitations or during recovery from surgery or illness.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Aids for Daily Living
benefit_group: Medical Items - Aids for Daily Living

description: A table-top vaporizer that produces steam or warm mist for respiratory relief. Used for congestion, croup, sinusitis, and respiratory conditions. Heats water to create steam that is inhaled for therapeutic benefit. Different from a humidifier in that it produces warm steam rather than cool mist. Compact tabletop size for bedside use.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Respiratory Equipment

description: Purchase of a Versa Frame - an adjustable toilet safety frame that fits around a standard toilet to provide support rails for sitting down and standing up. A freestanding frame with armrests that does not require permanent installation. Used by individuals with mobility issues, post-surgery recovery, or balance problems. Different from grab bars which are permanently mounted.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Aids for Daily Living
benefit_group: Medical Items - Aids for Daily Living

description: A blood test to measure the level of vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D) in the blood. Used to detect vitamin D deficiency or insufficiency, which is common in Canada due to limited sun exposure. Important for bone health, immune function, and mood regulation. Often ordered by physicians for patients with fatigue, bone pain, or depression symptoms.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests

description: Purchase of a non-wheeled walker (standard walker). A lightweight metal frame with four legs and rubber tips that must be lifted and placed with each step. Provides maximum stability for individuals with significant balance or weight-bearing issues. Used after surgery, for elderly mobility, or chronic conditions. Different from wheeled walkers which roll forward.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Mobility Aids

description: Purchase of a wheeled walker (rollator). A walking frame with wheels that rolls forward, making it easier to move than a standard walker. May have two or four wheels, hand brakes, a seat, and a basket. Used by individuals who need walking support but have enough balance to use wheels. More versatile than non-wheeled walkers for outdoor and longer-distance use.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Mobility Aids

description: Purchase of a wheeled commode - a portable toilet chair with wheels for easy repositioning. Combines the function of a commode (portable toilet) with wheels for mobility. Can often be used as a shower chair or rolled over a standard toilet. Different from stationary commode which has no wheels.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Aids for Daily Living
benefit_group: Medical Items - Aids for Daily Living

description: A medical wig (cranial prosthesis) for individuals who have lost hair due to medical conditions or treatments. Commonly needed after chemotherapy, radiation therapy, alopecia areata, or other medical hair loss conditions. Includes full wigs and partial hairpieces. May require a physician's prescription or letter of medical necessity.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Prosthetics

description: An X-ray diagnostic imaging procedure that uses radiation to create images of internal body structures, particularly bones. Used to diagnose fractures, dislocations, infections, tumors, and other conditions. Common X-rays include chest X-ray, limb X-rays for fractures, dental X-rays, and spinal X-rays. A basic and widely available imaging modality.
benefit_type: Medical Items and Services - Diagnostic Tests
